internship.title: Backend Web Development Internship
internship.description: A research-grounded, engineering-oriented internship focused on building, testing, securing, documenting and operating backend web services and REST APIs.

duration.guidance: Progress at a pace that allows each module task and the final project to be completed and reviewed; no fixed duration is imposed.

prerequisites: Programming fundamentals including variables, functions, control flow and basic data structures.
Basic SQL concepts are helpful but are taught and reinforced during the program.
objectives: Build backend services with a clear architecture.
Use TypeScript for maintainable backend code.
Validate input and handle errors safely.
Write automated tests and API documentation.
Apply security, performance and operational practices.
Use Git and Docker in a professional backend workflow.

technologyStack.name: Node.js
technologyStack.purpose: JavaScript runtime for the backend service.
technologyStack.role: Runs the HTTP API and application code.
technologyStack.why: It is a widely used server-side JavaScript runtime with official documentation covering HTTP servers, tests, streams and tooling.

technologyStack.name: TypeScript
technologyStack.purpose: Static type checking for JavaScript code.
technologyStack.role: Defines application and API types and catches many errors before runtime.
technologyStack.why: It improves maintainability of a multi-module backend without changing the runtime model.

technologyStack.name: Express 5
technologyStack.role: Maps HTTP requests to route handlers and middleware and centralizes error handling.
technologyStack.why: Its routing and middleware model is compact enough for interns to learn while still supporting realistic APIs.

technologyStack.name: PostgreSQL
technologyStack.role: Persists users, projects, issues and audit records with constraints and indexes.
technologyStack.why: It teaches relational modeling, transactions, constraints and query planning in a production-relevant database.

technologyStack.name: node-postgres (pg)
technologyStack.role: Executes parameterized SQL and transactions from the service layer.
technologyStack.why: It exposes SQL directly, making database behavior visible rather than hiding it behind an ORM.

technologyStack.name: Zod
technologyStack.role: Validates request bodies, query parameters and environment configuration.
technologyStack.why: Backend APIs must treat external input as untrusted; schema validation makes that boundary explicit.

technologyStack.name: JSON Web Tokens (JWT)
technologyStack.role: Carries authenticated user identity between requests.
technologyStack.why: It is useful for teaching stateless API authentication, while the internship also teaches token lifetime and secret management.

technologyStack.name: bcryptjs
technologyStack.role: Hashes and verifies passwords without storing plaintext credentials.
technologyStack.why: Password storage is a core backend security responsibility.

technologyStack.name: Vitest + Supertest
technologyStack.role: Tests services, middleware and API endpoints.
technologyStack.why: The internship must teach repeatable automated verification, not only manual requests.

technologyStack.name: Docker
technologyStack.role: Packages the API and runs PostgreSQL locally as a reproducible development stack.
technologyStack.why: Containerized backend development is directly supported by current Docker guidance.

phases.title: Quality and Operations
phases.focus: Testing, documentation, containers and operational engineering

modules.title: Backend Foundations and HTTP
modules.description: Build the mental model for a backend process, HTTP requests, responses, routing, middleware and API contracts before introducing persistence.
objectives: Explain the role of a backend runtime and HTTP server.
Read HTTP requests and responses including methods, status codes, headers and JSON bodies.
Design resource-oriented endpoints and middleware order.
Use Git for small, reviewable changes.

lessons.title: Backend responsibilities and request lifecycle
lessons.description: Understand what a backend service owns and how a request moves through an application.
learningObjectives: Distinguish transport, application and persistence responsibilities.
Trace a request from socket to response.
notes: A backend should have explicit boundaries: transport handling, validation, business logic and persistence. Keep framework-specific code at the edges.

lessons.title: HTTP methods, status codes and headers
lessons.description: Learn the HTTP semantics needed to design predictable APIs.
learningObjectives: Choose appropriate methods for common resource operations.
Choose meaningful success and failure status codes.
notes: HTTP status codes communicate outcome; response bodies should not be the only source of truth. Headers carry metadata such as content type and caching directives.

quiz.question: Which status best represents successful creation of a resource?
quiz.explanation: 201 explicitly indicates that a resource was created.

lessons.title: Express routing and middleware
lessons.description: Build an Express application using explicit routes and middleware.
notes: Express routing associates HTTP methods and paths with handlers. Middleware can modify requests/responses, terminate a request, or call next().

lessons.title: Git workflow for backend changes
lessons.description: Practice small commits, branches and reviewable changes.
learningObjectives: Write focused commits and inspect diffs before sharing work.
notes: A useful backend workflow separates requirement, implementation, verification and review. Never commit secrets or generated dependency directories.

practicals.title: Create and review a health endpoint
instructions: Run the server and request the endpoint.
Inspect git diff and commit the change.
practicals.expectedOutcome: A reviewable commit containing a working health endpoint.

tasks.title: Implement a health and readiness API
tasks.description: Add two operational endpoints to a small Express service.
tasks.problemStatement: The service has no machine-readable way to distinguish a live process from a process that can reach its database.
objectives: Implement GET /ready using an injected readiness check.
requirements: Return JSON and meaningful status codes.
constraints: Keep readiness logic outside the route handler.
tasks.hint: Keep the route thin; call a service that performs the readiness check.
tasks.solutionExplanation: The dependency is injected so the route can be tested without a real database. 503 communicates temporary unavailability for readiness.

modules.title: TypeScript, Configuration and Validation
modules.description: Turn a JavaScript-style service into a typed backend with explicit configuration and untrusted-input boundaries.
objectives: Use TypeScript types at module boundaries.
Validate HTTP input before business logic.

lessons.title: TypeScript for service boundaries
lessons.description: Use interfaces, type aliases and narrow types where data crosses modules.
learningObjectives: Avoid unsafe any at application boundaries.
notes: Types disappear at runtime, so runtime validation remains necessary for HTTP and environment input. TypeScript complements rather than replaces validation.

lessons.title: Environment configuration
lessons.description: Design startup configuration that fails early when required settings are absent.
learningObjectives: Keep secrets out of source control.
notes: Configuration should be read once, validated and passed into the application. Do not silently invent defaults for security-sensitive values.
lessons.code:
const port = Number(process.env.PORT ?? "3000");
if (!Number.isInteger(port) || port <= 0) throw new Error("PORT must be a positive integer");

lessons.title: Runtime validation with Zod
lessons.description: Validate JSON bodies and query parameters at the HTTP boundary.
learningObjectives: Translate validation failures into stable API errors.
notes: Reject unexpected or malformed input before it reaches SQL or business logic. Set reasonable request-size limits as part of the boundary.

lessons.title: Error taxonomy
lessons.description: Model validation, authentication, authorization, not-found, conflict and server failures distinctly.
learningObjectives: Map known failures to appropriate status codes.
Avoid leaking stack traces or secrets.
notes: Error handling belongs at the edge. Business code can throw typed application errors; one final error middleware maps them to safe responses.

tasks.title: Build a validated project-creation endpoint
tasks.description: Implement a typed endpoint that validates a project payload and returns a stable error shape.
tasks.problemStatement: Clients currently receive inconsistent failures when project names are missing or malformed.
objectives: Return 201 on success and 400 on invalid input.
Keep route, validation and service responsibilities separate.
tasks.hint: Define the input schema first, then write a small route adapter around the service.
tasks.solutionExplanation: The schema constrains type, length and project-key format before business logic executes. The route can catch ZodError and map it to the API error contract.

modules.title: PostgreSQL and Data Access
modules.description: Model relational data, write parameterized SQL, use transactions, constraints and indexes, and keep database access behind a clear service boundary.
objectives: Apply constraints, indexes and transactions appropriately.

lessons.title: Relational modeling
lessons.description: Translate backend entities into tables, keys, constraints and relationships.
notes: Database constraints are part of correctness. Application validation improves user feedback but should not be the only line of defense.

lessons.title: Parameterized SQL and pg
lessons.description: Execute SQL through node-postgres without string-concatenating untrusted input.
learningObjectives: Map database rows to domain objects.
notes: Parameter placeholders prevent user input from becoming SQL syntax. Connection pooling prevents opening a new database connection for every request.

lessons.title: Transactions and consistency
lessons.description: Use transactions for operations that must succeed or fail together.
learningObjectives: Identify when a transaction is required.
notes: A transaction groups multiple database steps into one all-or-nothing operation. Keep transactions short and avoid unrelated network calls inside them.

lessons.title: Indexes and query performance
lessons.description: Understand why indexes help selective lookups and why indexes also have costs.
learningObjectives: Use EXPLAIN when investigating a query.
notes: Do not add indexes blindly. Measure the actual query shape and data distribution before optimizing.

tasks.title: Implement transactional issue creation
tasks.description: Create an issue and an audit record atomically.
tasks.problemStatement: An issue must never exist without its corresponding creation audit record.
objectives: Insert the issue and audit record.
requirements: Commit only after both inserts succeed.
constraints: Use one client connection for the entire transaction.
tasks.hint: Acquire a client, BEGIN, perform both inserts, COMMIT, and ROLLBACK in catch/finally.
tasks.solutionExplanation: Both writes use the same database client and transaction. A failure in either statement causes rollback, preserving the invariant.

modules.title: Authentication and Authorization
modules.description: Implement secure account handling, authentication, authorization and ownership checks for an API.

lessons.title: Password storage
lessons.description: Understand why passwords must be hashed and how verification works.
learningObjectives: Never log or return password material.
notes: Password hashes are not reversible encryption. Use a password-hashing algorithm/library and keep the cost appropriate for the environment.

lessons.title: JWT authentication
lessons.description: Trace login, token issuance and authenticated request handling.
notes: JWT verification establishes that a token was signed by the trusted issuer; authorization is still a separate decision. Secrets belong in environment configuration.

lessons.title: Authorization and object ownership
lessons.description: Enforce permissions on both action and resource.
learningObjectives: Prevent users from reading or modifying another user’s object.
notes: A valid identity does not automatically grant access to every object. Every resource access must be evaluated against the authenticated principal and resource policy.

lessons.title: Authentication failure handling
lessons.description: Design safe responses and avoid account-enumeration and token leakage patterns.
notes: Do not put passwords, raw tokens or secrets in logs. Keep error messages useful without revealing protected implementation details.

tasks.title: Add authenticated issue ownership checks
tasks.description: Protect issue endpoints so a user can only mutate issues in projects they are allowed to manage.
tasks.problemStatement: A token currently proves identity but does not prevent cross-project access.
objectives: Load the target project and check membership/role.
Return 403 for authenticated users without permission.
requirements: Do not rely on a project ID supplied by the client as proof of access.
Keep authorization near the business operation.
constraints: Authorization must query trusted server-side data.
tasks.hint: Resolve the issue, its project and the user’s role before allowing mutation.
tasks.solutionExplanation: The check derives authorization from the stored project relationship rather than trusting a client-provided role or project identifier.

modules.title: API Design, Testing and Documentation
modules.description: Turn the service into a predictable API with pagination, filtering, automated tests and OpenAPI documentation.
objectives: Write unit and HTTP integration tests.

lessons.title: Resource-oriented API design
lessons.description: Organize endpoints around resources and consistent response semantics.
notes: API design is a contract. Avoid exposing database implementation details as the public contract unless intentionally chosen.

lessons.title: Pagination, filtering and sorting
lessons.description: Implement bounded list queries with deterministic ordering.
learningObjectives: Use limit/offset or cursor concepts appropriately.
notes: Never interpolate an arbitrary column name from user input. Validate page sizes and define deterministic ordering to make pagination repeatable.

lessons.title: Automated testing strategy
lessons.description: Separate unit tests from integration tests and define meaningful assertions.
learningObjectives: Test business rules without a database when possible.
Test critical HTTP paths against the real application boundary.
notes: Tests should verify observable behavior and security invariants, not internal implementation details.

lessons.title: OpenAPI and operational documentation
lessons.description: Document endpoints, schemas, authentication and failure responses.
learningObjectives: Document authentication requirements and common errors.
notes: OpenAPI provides a machine-readable description of an HTTP API. Documentation should stay aligned with implementation.

tasks.title: Implement paginated issue listing with tests
tasks.description: Add a bounded issue-list endpoint with filters and automated HTTP tests.
tasks.problemStatement: The issue list can return unbounded data and accepts unsafe sort parameters.
requirements: Do not concatenate raw user input into SQL.
constraints: Represent sort fields as a server-side mapping.
tasks.hint: Map public sort names to fixed SQL fragments and parameterize values.
tasks.solutionExplanation: Only the values are parameterized; the dynamic SQL fragments come from fixed server-side maps, preventing arbitrary SQL identifiers from entering the query.

modules.title: Production Engineering, Security and Operations
modules.description: Prepare a backend service for realistic deployment by addressing configuration, containers, logging, health checks, dependency security and operational failure modes.
objectives: Design structured logs and health checks.
Reason about graceful shutdown and production configuration.

lessons.title: Structured logging and request correlation
lessons.description: Make logs useful for debugging without exposing secrets.
notes: Logs should answer what happened, where, when and with which request context. Passwords, bearer tokens and secrets must never be logged.

lessons.title: Graceful shutdown and health checks
lessons.description: Close listeners and database pools predictably during termination.
notes: A production process should stop accepting new work, allow in-flight work to finish within a bound, and release resources.

lessons.title: Containerizing a Node API
lessons.description: Build and run the API in Docker with a separate database service.
notes: A container packages application dependencies and runtime. Do not bake secrets into an image.

lessons.title: Dependency and security review
lessons.description: Use dependency audit tooling and review API-specific threats.
learningObjectives: Run npm audit and interpret findings.
Map API controls to common OWASP risks.
notes: Dependency audit results are time-sensitive; remediate appropriately rather than blindly forcing major upgrades. API security includes authentication, authorization, input validation and resource controls.

tasks.title: Containerize and harden the service
tasks.description: Create a production-oriented container setup and document operational checks.
tasks.problemStatement: The service works locally but cannot be reproduced consistently and has no clear operational contract.
requirements: Do not put secrets in images or committed Compose files.
Use a non-root application user where practical.
constraints: Build the image, run it, then exercise the health endpoint from the container boundary.
tasks.hint: Use a multi-stage build: install dependencies, compile TypeScript, then copy only runtime artifacts into the final image.
tasks.solutionCode:
FROM node:22-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY tsconfig.json ./
COPY src ./src
RUN npm run build

FROM node:22-alpine
ENV NODE_ENV=production
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --omit=dev && npm cache clean --force
COPY --from=build /app/dist ./dist
USER node
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "dist/server.js"]
tasks.solutionExplanation: The build stage compiles TypeScript while the runtime stage contains only production dependencies and compiled output. Secrets remain runtime configuration.

modules.title: Independent Engineering Sprint
modules.description: Work from a realistic backlog, choose implementation order, verify behavior, review security and document decisions before the final project.
objectives: Break a backend requirement into implementation slices.
Review code for correctness, security and maintainability.

lessons.title: Requirement decomposition
lessons.description: Convert a backend requirement into acceptance criteria, data changes, API changes and tests.
notes: A good slice is independently verifiable and leaves the repository in a coherent state.

practicals.title: Decompose a change request
instructions: List schema, API, service and test changes.
Identify one security risk and one operational risk.
practicals.expectedOutcome: A small implementation plan that another engineer can review.

lessons.title: Debugging methodology
lessons.description: Use reproduction, instrumentation, hypothesis and regression testing instead of random edits.
learningObjectives: Use logs and targeted tests to isolate the cause.
notes: A useful debugging loop is reproduce → narrow → hypothesize → change → verify → regression-test.

lessons.title: Code review and technical documentation
lessons.description: Review a backend change for correctness and explain the important decisions.
learningObjectives: Identify correctness, security and performance issues.
Write a focused technical decision note.
notes: Review should prioritize user-visible correctness and risk. Documentation should explain decisions that are not obvious from code.

tasks.title: Perform a security and maintainability review
tasks.description: Review an API change for authorization, validation, SQL safety, error handling and test coverage.
tasks.problemStatement: A teammate submits a project-membership endpoint that trusts a role in the request body and concatenates a user-provided sort field.
objectives: Identify at least four concrete risks.
Add regression tests for the authorization boundary.
requirements: Base findings on actual API behavior and code.
Do not invent vulnerabilities unrelated to the code.
constraints: Trace every untrusted value from HTTP boundary to database or authorization decision.
tasks.hint: Trace each value from the request boundary to its authorization decision and SQL construction before deciding whether the change is safe.
tasks.solutionExplanation: The corrected version derives authorization from stored membership and maps dynamic SQL identifiers from a fixed allow-list. These controls address common API authorization and injection risks.

modules.title: Final Backend Engineering Project
modules.description: Demonstrate the complete backend engineering workflow by building, testing, securing, documenting and packaging the issue-tracking API.
objectives: Demonstrate automated verification and operational readiness.

lessons.title: Final project execution and evaluation
lessons.description: Use the final project specification as the authoritative assessment brief and prepare a reviewable repository.
learningObjectives: Execute the project plan in slices.
Prepare evidence for testing, security and design decisions.
notes: The final project is assessed as an engineering artifact: correctness, security, maintainability, tests, documentation and operational behavior all matter.

project.heading: Build a Production-Ready Issue Tracking REST API
project.description: Build a backend-only issue tracking service for small engineering teams. Authenticated users can belong to projects, create and manage issues according to project roles, search and paginate issues, and inspect an audit trail. The project consolidates HTTP API design, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, authentication, authorization, validation, testing, documentation, security and containerized operations.
project.problemStatement: A small engineering team needs a reliable API for tracking work without giving users access to projects or issues they do not control. The existing manual process provides no consistent validation, audit history, authorization boundary, or repeatable deployment. Build the service that would sit behind a web or mobile client.
objectives: Implement secure authentication and object-level authorization.
Persist relational data with constraints, indexes and transactions.
Expose a documented REST API with pagination and filtering.
Create automated unit and HTTP integration tests.
Package the service for reproducible local execution with Docker.

functional: Register a user with a unique email and securely hashed password.
Authenticate a user and issue a short-lived access token.
Create projects and manage project membership according to role.
Create, read, update and archive issues within authorized projects.
Support issue status and priority values enforced by application and database rules.
List issues with bounded pagination, status filtering and whitelisted sorting.
Record audit events for security-relevant project and issue mutations.
technical: Express 5 for HTTP routing and middleware.
node-postgres for parameterized SQL and transactions.
JWT access tokens with a server-side signing secret.
Vitest and Supertest for automated tests.
OpenAPI documentation for the HTTP contract.
Docker and Docker Compose for local reproducibility.
database: Users, projects, project_members, issues and audit_events tables.
Primary and foreign keys with appropriate uniqueness and check constraints.
Indexes supporting project issue lists and audit lookups.
Transactional issue creation with its audit event.
security: Never trust client-supplied roles or ownership claims.
Validate request bodies and query parameters.
Use parameterized SQL for values and fixed server-side mappings for dynamic SQL fragments.
Do not log passwords, bearer tokens or secrets.
Use secure environment configuration and a strong production JWT secret.
Return safe error responses without stack traces in production.
testing: Integration-test authentication, authorization, CRUD paths and error responses.
Test transaction failure behavior where practical.
deployment: Build a production image from a multi-stage Dockerfile.
Provide runtime environment variables separately from source control.
Run the API and PostgreSQL as separate services in Compose for local deployment.

features.name: Account registration
features.behavior: Accept a validated email and password, hash the password, and create a user while enforcing email uniqueness.

features.name: Login
features.behavior: Verify credentials and issue a short-lived signed access token without returning password material.

features.name: Project management
features.behavior: Create projects and maintain project membership with OWNER, MAINTAINER and MEMBER roles.

features.name: Issue lifecycle
features.behavior: Create, update and archive issues only when the authenticated user has permission in the containing project.

features.name: Issue search
features.behavior: Return bounded pages of issues with status filtering and a server-side whitelist for sort fields and direction.

features.name: Audit trail
features.behavior: Record important mutations with actor, action, entity type, entity ID and timestamp.

features.name: Operational endpoints
features.behavior: Provide liveness and database readiness endpoints with safe status responses.

architecture.dataFlow: Client → Express middleware → authentication/validation → route handler → application service → parameterized PostgreSQL query/transaction → mapped response → client
securityBoundaries: HTTP input is untrusted until validated.
Authentication establishes identity; authorization establishes permission.
Repository functions are the only layer that constructs SQL.
Configuration loads secrets at process startup and does not expose them to responses.

setupRequirements: Node.js supported by the current Node.js release line used for the internship project.
Docker Desktop or Docker Engine with Compose
A PostgreSQL client is optional because the database runs in the container.
implementationSteps: Initialize the TypeScript project and install runtime/development dependencies.
Create the PostgreSQL schema and indexes.
Implement a shared database pool and transaction helper.
Implement application error types and final error middleware.
Implement registration and login with password hashing and JWT verification.
Implement project membership and authorization policies.
Implement issue CRUD, filtering, pagination and transactional audit logging.
Add request-ID logging and health/readiness endpoints.
Write unit and HTTP integration tests for happy paths and security failures.
Write the OpenAPI contract and compare it with the running routes.
Build the Docker image and run API plus PostgreSQL through Compose.
Run tests, type-checking and npm audit; fix findings that apply.
Perform a manual security and consistency review.
Document startup, migrations, configuration, troubleshooting and rollback considerations.
testingPlan: Run unit tests for validation, error mapping and authorization policy.
Run integration tests against an isolated PostgreSQL database.
Verify 401 for missing/invalid credentials and 403 for authenticated but unauthorized users.
Verify 400 for malformed input and 409 for uniqueness conflicts.
Verify transaction rollback by forcing the audit insert to fail in a controlled test.
Verify health returns 200 and readiness changes when database connectivity is unavailable.
securityReview: Authentication and authorization are separate controls.
Object-level authorization is checked using trusted database relationships.
Passwords are hashed and never returned.
Dynamic SQL identifiers are selected from fixed server-side maps.
Request body size and schema validation are enforced.
Secrets are environment configuration, not source code.
Production errors do not expose stack traces.
Dependencies are checked with npm audit.
performanceReview: Use a connection pool rather than opening a connection per query.
Index issue lookups by project and common filter/order combinations after observing query patterns.
Bound page size to prevent unbounded result sets.
Use EXPLAIN ANALYZE on representative queries before changing indexes.
Measure latency and database time rather than claiming a benchmark without measurement.
deploymentGuidance: Provide production environment variables through the deployment environment or secret manager.
Run database migrations as a controlled release step.
Expose only the API port publicly; keep PostgreSQL on an internal network in real deployments.
Configure health/readiness checks with the deployment platform.
Keep a rollback plan for both application and database changes; prefer backward-compatible migrations when rolling deployments are used.

checks: Verify DATABASE_URL points to the Compose service hostname from inside the API container.
Confirm migrations ran against the expected database.
Confirm the same JWT secret is used for signing and verification.
Verify the stored role permits the action.
Do not trust a role supplied by the client.

fileWiseSolution.purpose: Defines runtime/development dependencies and repeatable scripts.
fileWiseSolution.explanation: The scripts make type-checking, tests and production builds explicit.
fileWiseSolution.code:
{
  "name": "issue-tracker-api",
  "private": true,
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "tsx watch src/server.ts",
    "build": "tsc -p tsconfig.json",
    "start": "node dist/server.js",
    "typecheck": "tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit",
    "test": "vitest run"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "bcryptjs": "^3.0.2",
    "express": "^5.1.0",
    "jsonwebtoken": "^9.0.2",
    "pg": "^8.16.3",
    "zod": "^4.1.5"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@types/bcryptjs": "^2.4.6",
    "@types/express": "^5.0.3",
    "@types/jsonwebtoken": "^9.0.10",
    "@types/node": "^24.3.0",
    "@types/pg": "^8.15.5",
    "supertest": "^7.1.4",
    "tsx": "^4.20.5",
    "typescript": "^5.9.2",
    "vitest": "^3.2.4"
  }
}

fileWiseSolution.purpose: Enables strict TypeScript compilation and emits runnable ESM JavaScript.
fileWiseSolution.explanation: Strict mode exposes unsafe assumptions early and the output directory is deterministic.

fileWiseSolution.purpose: Documents required runtime configuration without committing secrets.
fileWiseSolution.explanation: The example contains placeholders only; real values belong in the deployment environment.
fileWiseSolution.code:
PORT=3000
DATABASE_URL=postgres://app:change-me@localhost:5432/issue_tracker
JWT_SECRET=replace-with-a-long-random-secret
JWT_EXPIRES_IN=15m
NODE_ENV=development

fileWiseSolution.purpose: Loads and validates environment variables once at startup.
fileWiseSolution.explanation: Configuration failures should stop startup rather than become mysterious runtime failures.

fileWiseSolution.purpose: Creates the PostgreSQL connection pool and exposes a readiness check.
fileWiseSolution.explanation: The pool reuses database connections and centralizes database connectivity.

fileWiseSolution.purpose: Defines application errors with safe HTTP status mapping.
fileWiseSolution.explanation: Services throw typed errors and the final middleware decides how they are exposed to clients.

fileWiseSolution.purpose: Converts application and unknown errors into safe JSON responses.
fileWiseSolution.explanation: It is registered last so it can observe errors from earlier middleware and routes.

fileWiseSolution.purpose: Verifies bearer access tokens and attaches the authenticated user identity.
fileWiseSolution.explanation: Authentication is a middleware concern; authorization remains a service/policy concern.

fileWiseSolution.purpose: Adds a request identifier for correlation in logs and responses.
fileWiseSolution.explanation: The identifier is operational metadata and contains no secret material.

fileWiseSolution.purpose: Builds the Express application and registers middleware and routes.
fileWiseSolution.explanation: Keeping app construction separate from server startup makes HTTP integration tests easier.

fileWiseSolution.purpose: Starts the HTTP server and handles graceful shutdown.
fileWiseSolution.explanation: The process owns startup and termination; the app module remains testable without binding a port.

fileWiseSolution.purpose: Creates the relational schema, constraints and indexes required by the project.
fileWiseSolution.explanation: The database enforces important invariants even if another client bypasses the API.

fileWiseSolution.purpose: Centralizes reusable Zod schemas for authentication, projects and issues.
fileWiseSolution.explanation: These schemas define runtime input contracts before values reach services or SQL.

fileWiseSolution.purpose: Implements registration and login using bcrypt and signed access tokens.
fileWiseSolution.explanation: The service owns credential handling and does not return password hashes. Database uniqueness conflicts are mapped to a safe application error.

fileWiseSolution.purpose: Defines registration and login HTTP endpoints with runtime validation.
fileWiseSolution.explanation: Routes remain thin: parse input, call the service, and return the HTTP contract.

fileWiseSolution.purpose: Implements project creation and membership-aware project reads.
fileWiseSolution.explanation: The creator is inserted as OWNER in the same transaction as the project to avoid an ownerless project.

fileWiseSolution.purpose: Builds a small production image using separate build and runtime stages.
fileWiseSolution.explanation: The runtime stage installs only production dependencies and runs as the built-in node user.
fileWiseSolution.code:
FROM node:22-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY tsconfig.json ./
COPY src ./src
RUN npm run build

FROM node:22-alpine
ENV NODE_ENV=production
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --omit=dev && npm cache clean --force
COPY --from=build /app/dist ./dist
USER node
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "dist/server.js"]

fileWiseSolution.purpose: Runs the API and PostgreSQL together for reproducible local development.
fileWiseSolution.explanation: The database is reachable by service name from the API container; credentials are development-only example values.
fileWiseSolution.code:
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:18-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: app
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: app_password
      POSTGRES_DB: issue_tracker
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql
  api:
    build: .
    environment:
      PORT: 3000
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://app:app_password@db:5432/issue_tracker
      JWT_SECRET: change-this-development-secret-to-at-least-32-characters
      JWT_EXPIRES_IN: 15m
      NODE_ENV: development
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    depends_on:
      - db
volumes:
  postgres_data:

fileWiseSolution.purpose: Documents the public HTTP contract for the implemented endpoints.
fileWiseSolution.explanation: The document describes authentication, project creation, issue creation/listing and operational endpoints; it should be checked against the running service as routes evolve.
fileWiseSolution.code:
openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Issue Tracker API
  version: 1.0.0
servers:
  - url: http://localhost:3000
paths:
  /health:
    get:
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Service is alive
  /ready:
    get:
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Database is reachable
        "503":
          description: Database is unavailable
  /api/v1/auth/register:
    post:
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/Credentials'
      responses:
        "201": {description: User created}
        "400": {description: Invalid input}
        "409": {description: Email already registered}
  /api/v1/auth/login:
    post:
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/Credentials'
      responses:
        "200": {description: Token issued}
        "401": {description: Invalid credentials}
  /api/v1/projects:
    post:
      security: [{bearerAuth: []}]
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/ProjectInput'
      responses:
        "201": {description: Project created}
        "401": {description: Authentication required}
        "409": {description: Project key already exists}
  /api/v1/projects/{projectId}/issues:
    post:
      security: [{bearerAuth: []}]
      parameters:
        - {$ref: '#/components/parameters/ProjectId'}
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/IssueInput'
      responses:
        "201": {description: Issue created}
        "403": {description: Not authorized}
    get:
      security: [{bearerAuth: []}]
      parameters:
        - {$ref: '#/components/parameters/ProjectId'}
        - {name: page, in: query, schema: {type: integer, minimum: 1, default: 1}}
        - {name: pageSize, in: query, schema: {type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 100, default: 25}}
        - {name: status, in: query, schema: {type: string, enum: [OPEN, IN_PROGRESS, DONE, ARCHIVED]}}
        - {name: sortBy, in: query, schema: {type: string, enum: [createdAt, priority], default: createdAt}}
        - {name: direction, in: query, schema: {type: string, enum: [asc, desc], default: desc}}
      responses:
        "200": {description: Issue page}
        "403": {description: Not a project member}
components:
  securitySchemes:
    bearerAuth:
      type: http
      scheme: bearer
      bearerFormat: JWT
  parameters:
    ProjectId:
      name: projectId
      in: path
      required: true
      schema: {type: string, format: uuid}
  schemas:
    Credentials:
      type: object
      required: [email, password]
      properties:
        email: {type: string, format: email}
        password: {type: string, minLength: 12}
    ProjectInput:
      type: object
      required: [name, key]
      properties:
        name: {type: string}
        key: {type: string}
    IssueInput:
      type: object
      required: [title]
      properties:
        title: {type: string}
        description: {type: string}
        status: {type: string}
        priority: {type: string}

fileWiseSolution.purpose: Provides setup, configuration, testing and operational instructions for the project.
fileWiseSolution.explanation: The README is intentionally project-specific and points the intern to the migration and API contract rather than generic tutorials.
fileWiseSolution.code:
# Issue Tracker API

## Setup

1. Copy `.env.example` to `.env` for local non-container execution.
2. Install dependencies with `npm install`.
3. Apply `src/db/migrations/001_init.sql` to the PostgreSQL database.
4. Run `npm run typecheck`.
5. Run `npm test`.
6. Build with `npm run build` and start with `npm start`.

For the containerized workflow, run `docker compose up --build`. Apply the SQL migration to the `db` service before exercising protected endpoints.

## API

See `openapi.yaml` for the documented HTTP contract.

## Security

Do not commit `.env`, production JWT secrets, passwords or bearer tokens. Review `npm audit` findings before release.

## Operations

`GET /health` checks process liveness. `GET /ready` checks PostgreSQL connectivity.

principles: Evaluate observable engineering ability rather than memorization.
Require explanation of implementation and tradeoffs.
Do not treat passing tests as proof of security by itself.
Use the final project as the strongest evidence of integrated skill.
finalEvaluation: Explain the request lifecycle and architecture.
Implement or modify an authenticated API feature.
Explain and defend an authorization rule.
Run the automated test suite and interpret failures.
Explain the database transaction and indexing decisions.
Demonstrate the final project and explain its data flow.

researchNotes: The curriculum uses current official Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL and Docker documentation as primary technical references.
OWASP API Security guidance is used for API-specific security topics such as broken object-level authorization and input validation.
OpenAPI is included for machine-readable API documentation.
npm audit is included as a dependency-security workflow rather than as a guarantee that a project is vulnerability-free.
internship.qualityPolicy: No fabricated APIs, packages, benchmarks, test results, deployment results or company claims. Version-sensitive values must be verified against current official documentation before a production implementation is pinned.
